remaining_gaps: The authority delegated rests on Title II of the Second War Powers Act, 1942 (56 Stat. 177), whose expiry or termination is not shown by any held source: no statute text of Title II and no act extending or terminating it is held, the dossier chain lists no later order affecting EO 9610, and the Cruden number-citation lookup finds no held text citing it. Missing source: the text of Title II of the Second War Powers Act and the later act(s) fixing when its acquisition authority lapsed.

Paragraphs 1 and 2 end with the Board's sixty-day period (restarted by EO 9627 on 1945-09-24), but paragraph 3 also directs that the War Shipping Administration 'shall be guided by' the Board's determination 'to the extent provided by' EO 9387, and EO 9387 paragraph 5 makes the Administration guided by the Board's standards when determining just compensation for each vessel; no held source shows when that guidance direction ended (for example the Administration's termination or a revocation of EO 9387 or EO 9611). Missing source: the instrument ending the War Shipping Administration's duty to be guided by the Board's determination. The official page also still needs the page-image check the dossier flags (location confidence low).

The order runs 'until the termination of the present war or emergency, whichever is later'. No held source ties that phrase to a dated termination: the held 1964 U.S. Code Title 50 Appendix front matter (grade held_text_lead, not an original) lists Proclamation 2714 (cessation of hostilities, effective noon 1946-12-31), peace treaties and the 1951 joint resolution, but does not identify which war or emergency the 1945 order meant or when the later of them ended, and no rescission of the position is held. Missing source: an authenticated text fixing the emergency the order refers to and its termination date.

No held source dates the end of the appointments of Francis Biddle as Member and John J. Parker as Alternate Member of the International Military Tribunal (judgment and adjournment of the Tribunal, resignation or discharge), and no later order revoking or superseding EO 9626 is held; the dossier chain is empty. Missing source: a held instrument or record dating the end of the Member's and Alternate Member's service and of the assistance directed in paragraph 3.

Paragraph 4 makes possession of the Great Lakes Towing Company's system end when the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation determines it is no longer necessary; no held source records that determination or a return of the property (the Federal Register notice listed in the same issue only reports the taking of possession), and no later order ends it. Missing source: the Office of Defense Transportation order or Federal Register notice terminating possession, control and operation of the Great Lakes Towing Company, or a later Executive order.

The order amends EO 9547 to enlarge the powers of the Representative and Chief of Counsel and to vest the functions in a Chief of Counsel for War Crimes after the present Chief of Counsel vacates office; no held source shows when that office or the amended EO 9547 powers ended (no revocation of EO 9547 and no Military Governor order ending the Office of Chief of Counsel for War Crimes is held), and the held texts that cite EO 9679 are histories of the proceedings. Missing source: the instrument ending the Office of Chief of Counsel for War Crimes or revoking EO 9547.

The order adds the Los Angeles Union Stockyards Company to the plants that the Secretary of Agriculture may take possession of under EO 9685; the end of that possession (a termination order, release of the plants or revocation of EO 9685) is not shown by any held source, and the held texts naming EO 9685 are only the amending order and EO 9685 itself. Missing source: the instrument ending possession of the Los Angeles Union Stockyards Company plants or revoking EO 9685.

The order amends EO 9492 (as amended) by substituting 'two years' for 'eighteen months' in section 2(c) and adding section 3. The dossier chain lists later amendments of the same parent, EO 9792 (1946-10-23), EO 9840 (1947-04-22), EO 9867 (1947-06-23) and EO 9886 (1947-08-22), whose effect on section 2(c) and section 3 has not been established from their text, and no held source shows the end of EO 9492 or of the amended provisions. Missing: a reading of those four orders to see whether they restate the amended text, and an instrument ending EO 9492.

Paragraph 4 makes possession of the Monongahela Connecting Railroad Company's system end when the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation determines it is no longer necessary; no held source records that determination or a return of the property (the Federal Register notice in the same issue reports the taking of possession), and no later order ends it. Missing source: the Office of Defense Transportation order or Federal Register notice terminating possession, control and operation of the Monongahela Connecting Railroad Company, or a later Executive order.

The order restates many sections of EO 1888 of February 2, 1914, as amended, on conditions of employment in the service of the Panama Canal and the Panama Railroad Company; the dossier chain is empty and no held source shows when the amended sections ended (no revocation of EO 1888 or of the restated provisions, and no statute or treaty text ending the Canal Zone employment system, is held). Missing source: the instrument or statute ending the amended employment provisions.

The inspection authority is given 'for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of' Senate Resolution 71, 77th Congress, as continued by various Senate resolutions including Senate Resolution 55, 79th Congress; no held source shows when the Special Committee or its continuing resolutions ended, and no later order revokes the authority. Missing source: the Senate resolutions continuing the Special Committee to Investigate the National Defense Program and the date it ceased, or an order revoking the inspection authority.

The extension is of 'twenty-five years from the date on which any such trust would otherwise expire' for trusts expiring in 1947, so the end differs for each patent and no held source gives the expiry dates; later extension orders for later years, and statutory continuation of trust periods (the Indian Reorganization Act section 2, 25 U.S.C. 5102), are not held and could have extended or superseded the extension before its own maximum end of 1972-12-31. Missing sources: those later orders or statute text and the patent expiry dates.

The inspection authority is given for returns of 1941 to 1943 'for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of' House Resolution 154, 79th Congress, 1st session; no held source shows when that resolution's investigation or the Committee on Naval Affairs ended (the Legislative Reorganization Act of 1946 text abolishing the committee is not held), and no later order revokes the authority. Missing source: the text of House Resolution 154 and the statute or resolution ending the Committee on Naval Affairs, or an order revoking the authority.

Paragraph 5 ends the Amnesty Board upon the Attorney General's submission of its final recommendations to the President (unless otherwise provided by further Executive order); no held source gives the date of that submission or any further Executive order, and the submission date is an actual-performance fact, not a deadline. Missing source: a held record (the Board's report, a Presidential proclamation or the Attorney General's transmittal) dating the final submission.

The delegation concerns the President's powers under section 4(b) of the Joint Resolution approved December 30, 1947, which revived Title III of the Second War Powers Act for certain purposes; the Joint Resolution is not held, so when the revived authority lapsed is not shown, and EO 9919 (1948-01-03) only recites this order. Missing source: the text of the Joint Resolution approved December 30, 1947 and any act extending or ending the revived authority.

The designation lasts for the period of the members' service on the military tribunals established under Control Council Law No. 10; no held source dates the end of the tribunals or of these members' designations, and no later order revoking EO 9917 is held. Missing source: an instrument or record dating the end of the designations and of the tribunals' proceedings.
